goal: Locate single-month volume anomalies in offline_data/regional_sales.csv by computing each region×product_line monthly sales as a multiple of its own 24-month mean, report the top-3 combos with their multiples, months, and return rates, and judge whether each spike is more likely real demand or channel stuffing. Output a Markdown report saved to disk with source annotations, a data table, and a conclusion paragraph.

plan.title: Inspect CSV structure: Read offline_data/regional_sales.csv: list all column names, total row count, date range (min/max of the month column), and print first 5 rows as sample

Compute 24-month baseline & anomaly multiples: Using the CSV, for each (region × product_line) compute the 24-month rolling mean of monthly sales, then compute the ratio = month_sales / 24-month_mean for every month. Save the full result table to a CSV file (e.g. offline_data/anomaly_ratios.csv)

Identify top-3 anomalies & fetch return rates: From the anomaly_ratios.csv, find the top-3 (region × product_line × month) combinations with the highest ratio. For each, also extract the corresponding return_rate from the original CSV. Save a small summary table to offline_data/top3_anomalies.csv

Assess demand vs channel-stuffing signals: For each of the top-3 anomalies, compute auxiliary signals from the CSV: (a) return_rate for that month vs the 24-month average return_rate for the same combo, (b) whether the following month's sales dropped sharply (reversion), (c) whether the spike is isolated (1-month) or sustained (2+ months). Save a signal summary to offline_data/stuffing_signals.csv

Write Markdown report with embedded tables: Write a comprehensive Markdown report to offline_data/regional_sales_anomaly_report.md. Requirements: (1) H1 title; (2) at least one data table showing top-3 combos with ratio, month, return_rate; (3) every key number annotated with source in the format '（来源：offline_data/regional_sales.csv 的 <列名>，<聚合口径与样本行数>）' or '（来源：由前述两行计算）'; (4) a concluding paragraph judging whether each spike is more likely real demand or channel stuffing, citing the auxiliary signals; (5) no external data.
